Egypt’s chemical and fertiliser exports to India surged to $627 million in the first eight months of 2026, a 325 per cent increase from a year earlier. The jump, reported by Daily News Egypt and attributed to the Chemical and Fertilisers Export Council, lifted India to the third-largest destination for Egyptian shipments in the category.
Egypt’s chemical trade with India has moved from a niche flow to a fast-rising export lane, with shipments of chemicals and fertilisers leaping sharply in the first eight months of 2026. Daily News Egypt reported that the value reached $627 million, a rise that points to India’s growing role in Egypt’s external sales mix.Chemical and Fertilisers Export Council, marks a year-on-year increase of 325 per cent from $147 million in the same period of 2025. That translates into an additional $480 million in export value over just eight months, a jump large enough to reshape the ranking of destination markets for Egyptian producers.
India emerges as a larger outlet for Egyptian suppliers
The rise in exports also reflects a broader trend in commodity and industrial trade, where buyers in large emerging markets are increasingly sourcing from diversified suppliers. For Egyptian manufacturers, India offers scale, a large industrial base and demand across multiple downstream segments, from agriculture to manufacturing inputs. The latest numbers suggest that exporters have been able to capture a meaningful share of that demand, at least during the first part of the year.
What the export jump signals for the sector
Even so, the headline numbers point to a favourable external environment for Egyptian chemical and fertiliser suppliers. A higher export base to India can help producers diversify away from concentrated markets, improve plant utilisation and support foreign exchange earnings. For a sector tied closely to global commodity cycles, such a rise can also strengthen bargaining power with trading partners and logistics providers.

articles.summary: A three-year-old police Labrador whose arrival and training were funded by a $25,000 donation found a mis  The Times of IndiaHawaii Police Dog Finds Missing 70-Year-Old Hiker Near Volcano, He Now Wants To Adopt Her  NDTVHawai‘i Island Police K9 Trina Locates Endangered Missing Elderly Man in Hawai’i Volcanoes National Park  Hawaii Police Department (.gov)K-9 Trina locates missing man, 70, in Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park  KHON2Hawai‘i Police Department K...
articles.full_text:
A 70-year-old man who went missing while hiking in Hawaii Volcanoes National Park was found by a three-year-old police Labrador named Trina on Monday. According to the 
Hawaii Police Department
, authorities began searching for David Arai after he had not been seen for more than 24 hours. The dog eventually tracked him down about two miles from his rental vehicle, marking her second successful rescue in two months.
Arai, who lives on Oahu, was familiar with the national park and frequently explored its trails. His son, Kaohe, told local television station KHON2 that his father often went hiking alone. This time, however, his absence led to a search involving police officers, national park personnel and a helicopter.
By the time Trina found him at around 7.30 pm, the search had been under way for more than seven hours. Arai was lying slightly away from the trail, among bushes. He was subsequently carried to the trailhead and taken to Hilo Benioff Medical Center, where he received treatment for dehydration and exposure.
Trina, a Labrador Retriever originally from Sweden, had helped locate an endangered teenager in Waikoloa, just a month earlier. 
Arai now hopes to adopt the dog if she ever retires from police service.
The rescue operation
The search began after Puna patrol officers received a report about Arai at 12.16 pm on Monday. According to the police, he had last been known to be in the Volcano area, and nobody had seen him for over a day.
Investigators treated his disappearance as an endangered missing-person case after considering his age and information gathered during their investigation.
An important development came when officers found Arai's rental vehicle inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, which helped establish an area for the search.
Personnel from the police department and national park quickly began to search the surrounding area, while the Hawaii Fire Department deployed a helicopter to assist from above.
Officer Christopher Ross, who works with the department's Area II Juvenile Aid Section and joined the operation with Trina, told KHON2 that the conditions along the trail were difficult. Recalling how he first spotted Arai, he said the man was lying on his back in bushes, a short distance away from the trail itself.
“The conditions were pretty bad going down that trail. And the first thing I noticed, I saw the top of his head, and he was slightly off trail in the bushes, like pretty much lying on his back,” Ross said.
The officer also described Trina's reaction when they reached the missing hiker. The Labrador not just simply stopped after finding him, but it approached Arai and licked his hand.
“We led up to him, just wanted to make sure he was okay, and Trina, when she got next to him, she licked his hand basically to let him know that we found him and that he’s safe,” Ross said.
Who is Trina, the police dog behind the rescue?
Trina is trained as a live-find human tracking canine, a specialised police dog that helps locate missing people. She is also described as scent-discriminating, which means she can follow the scent of a particular individual.
Her work with the Hawaii Police Department involves searches for missing children and endangered adults across Hawaii Island.
Ross spoke warmly about his canine partner after Arai was found, describing how much her presence meant to him.
“I don’t think there are any words to describe it. It’s a blessing just having this dog. It really is. Like my last thought, last before I fell asleep, was that we truly have an angel on our hands," he added.
Missing hiker develops special connection with Trina
According to People magazine, Kaohe said his father was extremely grateful to the police department, park rangers and others who had participated in the operation. He was especially grateful to Ross and Trina, whose efforts ended the search.
After meeting Trina, he also became interested in the possibility of giving her a home once her working years were over. “And if she ever retires and is looking for an adoption, he’s open. He said he fell in love with that dog,” Kaohe said.

articles.title: India's Interest Rate Gap With G7 Economies Key To Attracting Foreign Debt Capital: YES Bank - Menafn
articles.summary: India's Interest Rate Gap With G7 Economies Key To Attracting Foreign Debt Capital: YES Bank  Menafn
articles.full_text:
The report said the interest rate gap with G7 economies is relevant for attracting foreign debt capital, particularly as the US Federal Reserve is expected to continue its rate-hiking cycle.
External member of the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), Saugata Bhattacharya, noted,“maintaining a certain gap between India and G7 interest rates is important for attracting debt capital flows,” ANI reported.
The assessment comes amid growing concerns over the domestic inflation outlook and the possibility of higher input costs being passed on to consumers. The October MPC meeting minutes showed that the RBI's inflation projection for the third quarter of FY27 had reached 6 per cent, the upper limit of its 2-6 per cent tolerance band.
YES Bank said September inflation data indicated a broader increase in prices, with both core inflation and core inflation excluding precious metals rising. The report also pointed to higher household inflation expectations and signs of businesses passing on increased input costs.
Growth Resilient, Inflation Risks Persist
Bhattacharya noted that demand pressures remained subdued, although the gap between actual economic activity and potential output appeared to be narrowing.
India's GDP grew 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of FY27, supported by private consumption, stronger exports and continued momentum in the services sector.
The report said some MPC members favoured a timely policy response to prevent current price pressures from spreading further across the economy. Higher energy prices, supply-chain disruptions and El Niño conditions were also identified as risks to the growth outlook.
YES Bank Expects 50 Bps Rate Hike
Based on domestic inflation risks and global monetary policy developments, YES Bank expects the RBI to raise the policy repo rate by a cumulative 50 basis points, comprising a 25-basis-point hike in December and another 25-basis-point increase in February.
The projection represents the bank's assessment and not an announced RBI decision. The report underscores the challenge for monetary policymakers in containing inflation while maintaining an interest rate differential that supports foreign debt capital flows.

articles.summary: Indian-origin man claimed ICE took his wife. Then, her burnt body was found buried  India TodaySee more headlines and perspectives on Google News
articles.full_text:
A man who claimed his missing wife had been taken by federal immigration authorities has been arrested and charged with her murder after her burned and buried remains were found about 70 miles from their home, authorities said.
An Indian-origin nurse and mother of an eight-month-old baby was found burned and buried in California, days after her husband told police that US immigration agents had taken her away from their home while she was collecting the mail. Her husband, Gurinder Gill, 28, has now been charged with her murder.
The 30-year-old victim, Jasmine Gill, was reported missing by her cousin on October 4, four days after she was last seen.
According to the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office, she and her husband were going through a divorce and a child custody dispute when she disappeared.
As investigators searched for Jasmine, Gurinder told the police that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents had arrested her outside their Sacramento home.
However, when detectives contacted the agency to verify his account, they were told that no enforcement activity had taken place at the residence.
"As the investigation progressed, Sacramento County Sheriff's Office detectives identified several inconsistencies in Gurinder's statements about his wife's disappearance," Sergeant Edward Igoe, a spokesperson for the sheriff's office, said in a statement.
The investigation took a grim turn on October 1, when authorities discovered burned and buried human remains in neighbouring El Dorado County, about 70 miles from the couple's home. The remains were later identified as those of Jasmine.
Deputies arrested Gurinder on October 14 and carried out search warrants at two homes associated with him. He is being held without bail.
Jasmine Gill became a registered nurse to follow in her mom's footsteps and had an 8-month-old. She was born in India, where her mother still lives, according to a GoFundMe campaign set up to support the family.
The fundraiser aims to help bring her remains back to her mother and support her eight-month-old son. Supporters have raised more than $21,000 to help return her remains to her mother and support her son.
"She was fighting for a better future for herself and her baby," the campaign said, adding that Jasmine had been seeking a divorce and a fresh start for herself and her child.
"Tragically, before she could build that future, Jasmine was murdered, leaving behind the very child she was fighting so hard to protect," it added.
